name: All-Party State Language Action Committee
role: All-party coordinating body of the Language Movement
contribution: The All-Party State Language Action Committee brought political parties, students, and activists together to coordinate the early 1952 campaign for recognition of Bangla as a state language.
context: The committee operated in Dhaka during January and February 1952, when organizers debated tactics, strikes, public meetings, and responses to Section 144. Its work linked earlier language-rights activism to the mass protest of 21 February.
impact: The committee provided a coordinating structure for collective action and helped turn a language demand into a broad public movement. Its history also shows the importance of coalition politics in the Language Movement.
highlight: All-party coalition that coordinated the 1952 campaign for Bangla's state-language recognition.
seoDescription: Learn how the All-Party State Language Action Committee coordinated parties, students, and activists during Bangladesh's 1952 Language Movement.
shortAnswer: The All-Party State Language Action Committee was the coalition that coordinated the Language Movement's early 1952 protests and demands.
searchAliases: All Party State Language Action Committee 1952

faq.question: What was the All-Party State Language Action Committee?
faq.answer: It was a coalition of political parties, students, and activists that coordinated the 1952 campaign for recognition of Bangla as a state language of Pakistan.

faq.question: Why was the committee important?
faq.answer: It gave the Language Movement an organizational framework for strikes, meetings, and collective decisions before the mass defiance of 21 February.
